items.reason: The unchecked lookup returns nil for unknown IDs, causing update and destroy to raise instead of returning not-found.
The normalization callback calls sub! on a nil host, raising before validation can report an error.
The alleged failure from returning false and then calling try(:category_id) is distinct from every golden-set issue.
The lookup lowercases only the database column, causing mixed-case URI hosts to fail matching.
The migration interpolates unescaped host values into SQL, allowing quotes to break the INSERT.
The migration dereferences the first query result without checking for an empty result, aborting before a fallback can work.
Unconditional map calls on null *_ids payloads describe a hydration failure absent from the golden set; this differs from the incorrect fruit fixture test.
The concern is database overhead from uncached host authorization queries, which no golden-set issue describes.
Unknown IDs produce nil records that update and destroy dereference without a not-found check.
A nil host reaches the normalization callback and causes sub! to raise instead of producing a validation error.
The comment includes the unchecked empty category-query result that crashes the migration, matching #07. It additionally reports the SQL interpolation problem covered by #06.
The migration preserves schemes and paths in stored hosts, which cannot match the new bare-host lookup.
The blank-host test passes because other prerequisites are false, so it does not test the condition named in its description.
Legacy host values are inserted without scheme/path normalization, breaking matching against URI.host after migration.
The query compares a lowercased column against an unchanged URI hostname, rejecting mixed-case URLs.
